doc.title: Anne Phillips interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 24, 2025

title: The art of accompanying singers
summary: She says accompanying a singer is an art not taught, praising Fred Hersch and Mike Renzi.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Yeah. It’s important to know in those situations what to leave out too, as an arranger.
Right? Stepping on the vocals and —

Absolutely. In fact one of the things that they don’t teach anywhere is how to be an accompanist to a pianist, as a pianist, how to accompany a singer. Because that’s an art in itself. And a lot of the young guys are not learning that at all and they’re all over the place. It was a story from NYU but they gave me somebody that my singer said, “I could sing that at my lesson but I can’t sing —” I said no wonder, I couldn’t come in on that intro in a million years because it was just all over the place and he’s playing filler and © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-

now come on, you’re supposed to make that singer — lift her up, make it wonderful. And there are very few young — Fred Hersch is one that has really taken the place of the Mike Renzis of the world. But there are not many guys around that really accompany well and they certainly don’t teach it in the schools.

At the end of this article I have from you, you used the word “joy” a lot. And you just made me think of it because a good accompanist has to be joyful in what they do. That has to bring them joy that they are assisting a musical performance.

Absolutely. You know and there are wonderful ones that do exactly that. And if you don’t feel that joy, if it’s — see a lot of pianists are there to show themselves off and so accompanying a singer is a dumb gig. That’s a foolish idea.
